name: Traditional Artisanal Production in India
description: Introduction to indian artisanal traditions: an overview. Historical and cultural contexts of artisanal production. Indigenous materials and sustainable techniques: wood, metal, stone, clay, textiles, colors. Knowledge systems and role of community learning. Craft and aesthetics: Indian theories of beauty - rasa, bhava and auchitya. Tools, techniques, and rhythms of making. Sustainability, ecology, and zero-waste in traditional craft. Artisan economies: trade, guilds, markets - ancient to modern. Colonial impact and post-independence revivals. Intellectual property and GI tags in traditional knowledge. Design thinking for the artisanal sector: co-creation and innovation. Policy, livelihoods and digital access for artisans. Craft and gender: roles, agency, and representation. Immersion, observations and interactions with an Artisanal community. Exploration and co-framing of new opportunity pathways with Artisanal communities. Applying design thinking approaches to collaboratively Ideate diverse solution pathways to overcome challenges. Using business model canvas and value proposition canvas to propose new technology - business - design approaches for revitalization of Artisanal cluster. Self study components include ethnographic immersion and research methods as well as recording, editing and production of audio-video and creation of Blog, website, app of outcomes and solutions for the artisanal sector.
